item.text:
## 1B.3 Research Note: Narendra Modi in 2024

**Assessment:** The 2024 record shows **some support** for strengthened nuclear safety discipline, but mostly through **institutional oversight of civilian reactors** rather than a clearly new Modi-led reform to weapons custody or command-and-control. I found **no direct 2024 public evidence** of a change to India’s nuclear command authority, custody rules, or emergency-control architecture.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **AERB grants permission for First Approach to Criticality of 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor** | Atomic Energy Regulatory Board / PIB | 30 Jul 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2039099&lang=2&reg=48 | India’s nuclear safety regulator said it approved first criticality only after phased core loading, multi-tier safety review, site inspection, and resident-observer oversight. This is strong evidence of **accident-prevention discipline** and controlled reactor custody. | 1B.3 |
| **India’s Nuclear Safety Regulator Approves the First Approach to Criticality of RAPP Unit 7** | Department of Atomic Energy / PIB | 11 Sep 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2053660&lang=2&reg=48 | AERB said permission came only after satisfactory safety reviews and that the resident site-observer team would continue monitoring commissioning. This supports a finding of **tight safety governance** rather than lax handling. | 1B.3 |
| **No discrepancies in operational safety in Indian nuclear power plants** | Department of Atomic Energy / PIB | 31 Jul 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2039693 | The minister said reactors are operated by highly trained, AERB-licensed personnel and that procedures are periodically reviewed and upgraded. This is direct evidence of **operational safety controls** and routine command discipline. | 1B.3 |
| **India’s Nuclear Power Plant Safety Beyond Doubt: Dr. Jitendra Singh** | Department of Atomic Energy / PIB | 5 Dec 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2081169 | The minister emphasized stringent safety protocols and international oversight, reinforcing the public line that India’s nuclear-energy sector remained under robust safeguards. This supports **custody and safety assurance**, though it is not a Modi-specific policy change. | 1B.3 |
| **Inter-Services Organisations (Command, Control & Discipline) Act notified through Gazette Notification** | Ministry of Defence / PIB | 10 May 2024 | https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2020222 | This is not nuclear-specific, but it does show the government moving to bolster **command, control, and discipline** in the armed forces. It is only indirect evidence for 1B.3 because it does not address nuclear custody or accident prevention directly. | 1B.3 |

### What I did **not** find
- No 2024 primary-source announcement of a new **nuclear command-and-control reform**, revised **custody procedures**, or updated **accident-response doctrine** tied to Modi personally.
- No evidence of a deliberate weakening of safeguards in 2024.
- The public record is therefore **safety-maintenance heavy**, not **safeguard-enhancement explicit**.

### Bottom line
The best-supported conclusion is **modest positive evidence** for 1B.3, driven by regulator-led safety approvals and official assertions of disciplined reactor operations. But the evidence is **institutional and civilian**, not a clear Modi-led strengthening of nuclear command-and-control or weapons custody.
